newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HAND GRENADES DAMAGE BUDAPEST SHOPS, POLICE SAY.
newsitem.headline: HAND GRENADES DAMAGE BUDAPEST SHOPS, POLICE SAY.

text.p: Two hand grenades were detonated in Budapest early on Monday, damaging two shops in the second bombing in the Hungarian capital over the weekend.
The two grenades exploded at about 1:30 a.m. in a commercial section of the city, blowing out the windows of an automobile showroom and a small restaurant but causing no injuries, police said.
National police spokesman Laszlo Garamvolgyi said police were investigating but declined to speculate on the reasons for the bombings.
Hungary has been hit by a rash of bombings this year, including another over the weekend in which a hand grenade was used to blow up a luxury car in Budapest.
The car, heavily damaged early on Saturday, belonged to a man identified only as Adam M., 35, who operated games arcades and gambling machines, the national news agency MTI said.
Police said the bomb probably had been planted by competitors to intimidate the victim.
Earlier this month a small bomb exploded in a dustbin near Budapest's Dohanyi Utca Synagogue, Europe's largest synagogue. The blast scattered trash but caused no other damage.
As of mid-October, the Hungarian press reported that police were investigating 13 explosions of hand grenades and other devices this year, compared to 28 blasts in the preceding seven years.
Police have said that most bombings in Hungary are linked to criminal attacks or suicide attempts. They say they have no evidence of terrorist groups operating in the country.
